title: Ang 1333–1348: the Gurus in Prabhati
hookLine: dawn hymns of the third, fourth and fifth Gurus
tomorrow: before anyone had a religion, what came first?

lines: A DARK DORM ROOM, TWO ALARMS.
SO YOU WEREN'T THE ONLY ONE AWAKE.
cards: A dorm room, still dark, two beds, boxes everywhere. Hana's alarm goes off before dawn. A minute later, Simran's does.
Hana sits up, a little embarrassed. I saw yours on your phone last night, she says. I didn't want you to be the only one awake on the first morning in a strange place.
She doesn't pray. She just sits on her bed with a cup of tea, while Simran opens the Granth to the dawn.

teach.b: After Guru Nanak, Prabhati belongs to the third, fourth and fifth Gurus, from ang 1333 on. Their dawn hymns keep the hour he opened: the Name, sung while it's still dark, the work of amrit vela. Now hold up the fortnight.
A key, given, for the mind's locked room. Earn, eat, give.
The company you keep. Rain on a dry field, and one storm with two sides.
A temple that turned, and every job holy. A night raga that opens green. No enemy, no stranger.

teach.h: A MIRROR, A PARENT, THE DAWN.
teach.b: One face in every mirror. Father and mother in one breath.

And the dawn. Here's something to tell a friend tonight: not two weeks ago, the roommate across this dorm room with her tea was a checkbox on a housing form. Simran reads ang 1335 by the light of her phone.
Hana blows on her tea. Neither says much. Outside, it's getting light.

how: Prabhati hymns are sung in kirtan in the early morning; after Guru Nanak's, readers find the hymns of Mahala 3, 4 and 5 in turn under their headings.

games.q: an older driver at your dad's company says his work is 'nothing special.' which line from these two weeks fits best?
o: every job is holy: Ravidas named his family's work in the Granth.
burn the world's praise, so his work shouldn't matter to him.
night and green: he should rest more and work a little less.
games.why: on ang 1293 Ravidas names his family's trade, carrying dead cattle, and the Gurus kept it in the Granth. every job is holy.

practice: If you can, stand and walk slowly to a window, or across the room and back, letting each step land with one breath. Then sit for the rest of the time with your eyes open, as if the day hasn't quite started yet.
